items.q: What is Omni?
items.a: A native macOS app that searches your files by meaning. An on-device embedding model indexes text, PDFs, images, audio, and video into one vector space, and search ranks files by similarity to your query.

items.q: What does Omni download on first launch?
items.a: The embedding model, about 1.9 GB, from Hugging Face. The OCR model (about 4.5 GB) is an optional second download. Both are stored in ~/Library/Application Support/Omni.

items.q: How do I choose what gets indexed?
items.a: Click Add... in the sidebar's Index section and pick one or more folders, or your Photos library. New sources start indexing right away.

items.q: Where is the list of keyboard shortcuts?
items.a: Help > Omni Keyboard Shortcuts, or ⌘/.

items.q: How do I search?
items.a: Press ⌘F to focus the search field and describe what you are looking for. Results update as you type; turn off Search as you type in Settings > Performance to search only on ↩.

items.q: Does Omni also match file names?
items.a: Yes. When a query looks like a file name (it has an extension, or is a few uncommon words), matches from a file-name index are merged into the ranking. The filename: qualifier matches names explicitly.

items.q: Can I search with a file or image instead of text?
items.a: Yes. Drag a file, image, or text onto the results area, paste one with ⌘V, or choose File > Search by a File... (⇧⌘O). A "Searching by" chip shows the source; its X clears it.

items.q: How do I find files similar to a result?
items.a: Select the result and press ⌥⌘F, or right-click and choose Find similar. The chip then reads "Similar to".

items.q: Why are some results stacked?
items.a: Identical copies of a file always collapse into one result, and near-identical files do too by default. Show copies expands a stack; turn off Stack near-identical results in Settings > Performance to stack only identical copies.

items.q: Which key:value qualifiers can I type?
items.a: type: (image, video, audio, text, scanned), tag:, ext:, in: (a folder), filename:, date: (week, month, year), after: (7d, 2w, 3m, 1y), score: (for example 70%), and sort: (relevance, name, date). The rest of the text is the semantic query.

items.q: How do I combine or exclude filters?
items.a: Separate values with commas (type:image,video) and prefix a minus to exclude (-type:audio, -in:~/Library). Repeated tag: or in: qualifiers match any of them. Quote values with spaces: in:"~/My Documents".

items.q: How do I search for text that looks like a filter?
items.a: A qualifier needs a known key and a value right after the colon, so 12:30, URLs, and "type: theory" stay in the query. When the query does contain a qualifier, As plain query in the filter menu embeds the text exactly as typed.

items.q: What does the filter menu do?
items.a: The funnel button next to the results filters by file type, folder, extension, date, and relevance, and writes the result back into the search field as qualifiers. Clear filters resets them.

items.q: Why do some searches show "No results above 50%"?
items.a: By default only strong matches are shown: a 50% floor, scaled per file type. Click Show N weaker matches, or set Relevance to All in the filter menu.

items.q: How do I open or preview a result?
items.a: ↩ or ⌘O opens the selection in its default app. Space or ⌘Y opens Quick Look.

items.q: What is on a result's context menu?
items.a: Open, Quick Look, Transcribe, Find similar, Generate Tags, Reveal in Finder (⇧⌘R), Copy path (⌥⌘C), Share, Move to Trash (⌘⌫), and Ignore folder. Most are also in the File menu, where the shortcuts work.

items.q: How do I change the view or sort order?
items.a: ⌘1 for gallery, ⌘2 for list. View > Sort by, or the toolbar, sorts by Relevance (default), Name, or Date modified.

items.q: What do "Page 3" or "Line 1240" on a result mean?
items.a: Where the best-matching passage is in the file: a page for PDFs, a line for text and code. In list view, a text result expands to show its matching passages. The percentage is cosine similarity, shown as 0-100%.

items.q: What happens when I click a folder in the sidebar?
items.a: It opens a Finder-style browser of that folder's indexed files and scopes search to it. Double-click descends; Go > Enclosing Folder (⌘↑) goes up, and ⌘[ / ⌘] go back and forward.

items.q: How do I search several folders at once?
items.a: Right-click a folder and choose Add to Search Scope, or type several in: qualifiers.

items.q: How do I pause or remove a folder?
items.a: Right-click it: Pause this folder stops indexing it and keeps its files searchable; Remove from Omni drops its files from the index. Removing a subfolder adds an ignore rule instead.

items.q: Can Omni index my Apple Photos library?
items.a: Yes. Choose Add... and pick the Photos library, then index the whole library or selected albums. Photos and videos are indexed; items stored only in iCloud are counted in Settings > Storage as Photos not on this Mac.

items.q: Is the index kept up to date?
items.a: Yes. Omni watches indexed folders with FSEvents and re-embeds only new or changed files. File > Update Index (⇧⌘I) runs a pass by hand.

items.q: How are long documents and scanned PDFs handled?
items.a: Text is read up to 2 MB per file and split into chunks, all of which are indexed. A PDF with no text layer is indexed page by page as images.

items.q: How do I exclude files or types?
items.a: Settings > Files turns whole file types on or off and chooses whether iCloud files that are not downloaded are skipped. Settings > Content has minimum sizes per type and ignore rules in .gitignore syntax.

items.q: What are image and video tags?
items.a: Short labels such as "cat, couch, crib", generated on your Mac while images and videos are indexed. Search them with tag:beach or exclude with -tag:beach. Turn tagging off in Settings > Content.

items.q: What is the folder map?
items.a: Right-click a folder and choose Visualize > UMAP or PCA to lay out its indexed files in 2D by embedding similarity. Clicking a file highlights its 10 nearest neighbors; the map reads existing vectors and embeds nothing.

items.q: What is the OCR workspace?
items.a: A mode that transcribes PDFs and images to Markdown on your Mac with the jina-ocr-v1 model: tables as HTML, formulas as LaTeX. Toggle it with the toolbar button or ⌥⌘O. Indexing pauses while a document is transcribed.

items.q: How do I open a document to transcribe?
items.a: Drop a PDF or images on the workspace, paste an image, or press ⌘O. From search results, choose Transcribe (⌥⌘T).

items.q: How do I save or share a transcript?
items.a: Save Markdown... (⌘S) writes a .md file, Copy Markdown (⇧⌘C) copies it, and Share... sends it.

items.q: Can I search inside a transcript?
items.a: Yes. ⌘F finds text in the document; ⌘G and ⇧⌘G step through matches. Edit > Search for Selected Text (⌥⌘E) searches your index with the selection.

items.q: Are transcripts cached?
items.a: Yes. Pages are saved as Markdown and reused until the file or the model changes. The cache location and switch are in Settings > OCR.

items.q: How does search history work?
items.a: Settled searches appear in the sidebar under Today, Yesterday, Previous 7 Days, Previous 30 Days, and Earlier. Clicking one re-runs it with its filters.

items.q: How do I bookmark a search?
items.a: Press ⌘D or click the star in the toolbar. Bookmarks are pinned at the top of the sidebar and never pruned.

items.q: How do I control what is recorded?
items.a: Settings > History: Add searches to history (Automatically, When I press Return, or Only when I bookmark), Save serving history for agent and API searches, and Keep history for 3, 7, 14, or 31 days (default 31). Clear... removes all recents and keeps bookmarks.

items.q: How is Settings organized?
items.a: Seven tabs: Files, Content, Performance, Storage, OCR, History, and Serving.

items.q: How do I trade indexing speed for detail?
items.a: Settings > Performance: Max image size (1024-2048 px, default 1568), Max frames per video (6, 16, or 32, default 32), and Characters per chunk (1200-3600, default 1800).

items.q: What does Maximum memory do?
items.a: It caps the memory the models and their buffer cache use, not the whole app. The first-launch default is 40% of RAM, between 2 and 6 GB; Off means unlimited. A live breakdown of Omni's memory is shown below it.

items.q: Which embedding models are available?
items.a: Omni Nano (downloaded on first launch) and Omni Small (about 1.7B parameters, higher quality). Switch in Settings > Storage; switching rebuilds the index.

items.q: Can I move the index?
items.a: Yes. Settings > Storage > Location > Change... copies the index to another folder, such as an external drive, and leaves the old copy for you to delete.

items.q: Does anything leave my Mac?
items.a: Indexing, search, tagging, and OCR run locally on the GPU. Network use is limited to model downloads, a daily update check, and the optional benchmark. Results are uploaded only if you turn on Share results.

items.q: What does Run benchmark do?
items.a: Settings > Performance > Run benchmark indexes a fixed 300-file dataset in isolation and reports files per second and peak memory. Your index is not touched, and indexing resumes afterwards.

items.q: How are updates delivered?
items.a: Omni checks once a day on launch and prompts when a newer version exists. Omni > Check for Updates... checks now.

items.q: What does Serving do?
items.a: It runs a local HTTP server (default port 51234) with /v1/search, embedding endpoints, OCR endpoints, source management under /v1/sources, and an MCP endpoint at /mcp. Turn it on in Settings > Serving or with the toolbar's network button.

items.q: How do I connect Claude Code or another MCP client?
items.a: In Settings > Serving, click MCP for a ready-made config, for example: claude mcp add --transport http omni http://127.0.0.1:51234/mcp.

items.q: Which MCP tools are available?
items.a: Nine: search, search_inline, file_status, tag_image, ocr, list_sources, add_source, pause_source, and remove_source. They return paths, scores, snippets, tags, and transcripts; agents read files with their own tools.

items.q: What is the SKILL.md button for?
items.a: It generates a skill file documenting the HTTP API with your port and token filled in, for agents that follow written instructions. Save it where your agent reads skills, such as ~/.claude/skills/omni-local-search/SKILL.md.

items.q: Which embedding APIs are supported?
items.a: OpenAI and Jina (/v1/embeddings), Cohere (/v1/embed, /v2/embed), and Gemini (:embedContent, :batchEmbedContents). Each honors its query or document role, such as input_type or taskType; a missing role means document.

items.q: Can I run OCR over the API?
items.a: Yes. /v1/chat/completions takes the OpenAI chat shape with streaming, /v1/ocr takes Mistral's OCR shape with page selection, and MCP has an ocr tool (10 pages per call). Documents are sent as data: URIs or local paths; remote URLs are not fetched.

items.q: Is the server safe to expose?
items.a: By default it listens on this Mac only. Local network access always requires a bearer token, generated if none is set. Path arguments are limited to indexed folders.
